title: Quantum Complexity of Hidden Shift over Cyclic Groups
summary: The known Kuperberg algorithm provides a subexponential quantum baseline, but whether cyclic Hidden Shift has an efficient algorithm or is quantum-hard remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the Hidden Shift problem over the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/N$, determine whether an efficient quantum algorithm exists beyond the known Kuperberg algorithm with running time $2^{O(\sqrt{\log N})}$, or establish evidence that the problem is quantum-hard. This unresolved algorithmic question matters because an efficient quantum algorithm for Hidden Shift over $\mathbb{Z}/N$ would yield efficient quantum attacks on important public-key cryptosystems, including prime candidates for quantum security and the eventual replacement of RSA in Internet cryptography.

scope.domain: Quantum algorithmic complexity of the Hidden Shift problem over cyclic groups.
parameters: N, the parameter defining the cyclic group Z/N
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether an efficient quantum algorithm exists beyond the known Kuperberg algorithm, or establish evidence that Hidden Shift over Z/N is quantum-hard.

progress.summary: The source presents Hidden Shift over Z/N as an unresolved algorithmic problem despite Kuperberg's known algorithm, and emphasizes the cryptographic significance of possible efficient quantum algorithms.
